assignedReviews.card_evidence: Brushing scrubs the sticky plaque off your teeth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about dental hygiene and plaque removal, not about how any of the listed body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. Teeth are part of the digestive system, but the card does not describe digestive system function; it only discusses brushing to remove plaque.

copy.en: Brushing scrubs the sticky plaque off your teeth — that's why it's important to brush twice a day so it doesn't build up!
copy.tl: Inaalis ng pagsisipilyo ang malagkit na plaque sa ngipin — kaya mahalagang magsipilyo nang dalawang beses sa isang araw para hindi ito magtipon!
copy.bis: Ang pagsipilyo mokuha sa pilit nga plaque sa ngipon — mao nga importante nga magsipilyo kaduha sa usa ka adlaw aron dili kini motipon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Plastic bottles can be made into creative items like dolls or airplanes instead of being thrown away.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about reusing plastic bottles to make toys, a recycling/reuse idea. It does not address factors affecting rates of chemical reactions or any application to food preservation, materials production, fire control, pollution, or corrosion.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Plastic bottles can be made into creative items like dolls or airplanes instead of being thrown away.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes crafting toys from plastic bottles, not the formation or breaking of chemical bonds or chemical change. No chemistry content is present.

copy.en: Plastic bottles can be made into creative items like dolls or airplanes instead of being thrown away.
copy.tl: Ang mga plastic bottle ay pwedeng gawing malikhaing bagay tulad ng manika o eroplano imbes na itapon.
copy.bis: Ang mga plastic bottle pwede himoon nga malikhain nga mga butang sama sa monyeka o eroplano imbes nga ilabay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Plastic is a thermal insulator
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about plastic as a thermal insulator, which is a physics/materials topic. G4-L-6 requires grouping animals by their diet (herbivores, carnivores, omnivores). There is no connection to animal food groups.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Plastic is a thermal insulator
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw a simple food chain using living things from the Philippines and label them as herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores
assignedReviews.reason: G4-L-7 requires drawing a food chain of Philippine living things labeled by feeding type. The card discusses heat transfer and insulation, completely unrelated to food chains or living things.

copy.en: Plastic is a thermal insulator, so it does not feel hot or cold easily and does not transfer heat efficiently.
copy.tl: Ang plastic ay thermal insulator, kaya hindi ito agad umiinit o lumalamig at hindi mahusay maglipat ng heat.
copy.bis: Ang plastic usa ka thermal insulator, busa dili dayon kini moinit o mobugnaw ug dili episyente sa pagbalhin ug heat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Convergent boundaries are destructive zones where two tectonic plates move toward each other and collide.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes convergent plate boundaries (tectonic plate collision), which is an Earth science topic. G9-F-10 is about electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy created by vibrating charged particles traveling as transverse waves. There is no overlap in subject matter; the card provides no information about EMR.

copy.en: Convergent boundaries are destructive zones where two tectonic plates move toward each other and collide.
copy.tl: Ang convergent boundaries ay mga destructive zone kung saan ang dalawang tectonic plate ay kumikilos palapit sa isa't isa at nagbabanggaan.
copy.bis: Ang convergent boundaries mao ang mga destructive zone diin ang duha ka tectonic plate molihok paduol sa usag usa ug magbangga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: platypus venom
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the toxicity of platypus venom to humans, which is unrelated to animal adaptation (mimicry, camouflage) or how animals change to suit their environment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: platypus venom
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about venom effects, not about which animal groups reproduce by live birth versus laying eggs.

copy.en:
Is platypus venom deadly to humans?

No -- it's extremely painful, but platypus venom does not usually kill a person.
copy.tl:
Nakamamatay ba ang kamandag ng platypus sa tao?

Hindi -- napakasakit nito, pero hindi ito karaniwang nakakamatay ng tao.
copy.bis:
Makamatay ba ang hilo sa platypus sa tawo?

Dili -- hilabihan kasakit, apan dili kini kasagaran makamatay sa tawo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pluto is two-thirds the size of Earth's moon
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how plate tectonics can be used to explain the formation of the largest mountain ranges on Earth including the Himalayas and the Andes mountains
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes Pluto's size, surface, and moons. It provides no information about plate tectonics or the formation of mountain ranges such as the Himalayas and Andes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pluto is two-thirds the size of Earth's moon
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the location and distribution of active volcanoes, earthquake epicenters, and major mountain belts to the distribution of oceanic crust and continental crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about Pluto, not about the distribution of volcanoes, earthquake epicenters, or mountain belts relative to oceanic and continental crust.

copy.en: Pluto is two-thirds the size of Earth's moon, its surface is covered with nitrogen, and it has three known moons: Charon, Hydra, and Nix.
copy.tl: Ang Pluto ay two-thirds ng laki ng buwan ng Earth, ang surface nito ay natatakpan ng nitrogen, at mayroon itong tatlong kilalang buwan: Charon, Hydra, at Nix.
copy.bis: Ang Pluto two-thirds sa gidak-on sa bulan sa Earth, ang surface niini natabonan sa nitrogen, ug aduna kini tulo ka nailhan nga bulan: Charon, Hydra, ug Nix.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Polluting air and water interferes with the balance of nature
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses pollution and its effect on nature's balance, which is unrelated to examining a local weather chart, interpreting local weather, or practicing safety precautions for poor/extreme weather. No direct or prerequisite support for the competency.

copy.en:
What human activity interferes with the balance of nature?

Polluting air and water interferes with the balance of nature and harms living things.
copy.tl:
Anong gawain ng tao ang nakakasira sa balanse ng kalikasan?

Ang pagpaparumi sa hangin at tubig ay nakakasira sa balanse ng kalikasan at nakakasama sa mga may buhay.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga kalihokan sa tawo ang makaguba sa balanse sa kinaiyahan?

Ang paghugaw sa hangin ug tubig makaguba sa balanse sa kinaiyahan ug makadaot sa mga buhing butang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pollution from discarded non-biodegradable materials, oil spills, sewage, and toxic chemicals like lead and mercury poses a serious threat to estuarine plants and animals.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes pollution threats to estuarine organisms, not the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It does not support identifying basic needs.

copy.en: Pollution from discarded non-biodegradable materials, oil spills, sewage, and toxic chemicals like lead and mercury poses a serious threat to estuarine plants and animals.
copy.tl: Ang polusyon mula sa mga itinapong non-biodegradable materials, oil spills, sewage, at mga nakakalasong kemikal tulad ng lead at mercury ay seryosong banta sa mga halaman at hayop sa estuary.
copy.bis: Ang polusyon nga naggikan sa mga gilabay nga non-biodegradable materials, oil spills, sewage, ug makahilo nga mga kemikal sama sa lead ug mercury usa ka seryoso nga hulga sa mga tanom ug mananap sa estuary.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Every protein is made of one or more polypeptides
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains protein structure (polypeptide chains, amino acids, peptide bonds) and has no connection to soil formation from rocks and minerals. It does not support any part of the competency.

copy.en: Every protein is made of one or more polypeptides, which are chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds, and the amino acid sequence determines how the protein folds.
copy.tl: Ang bawat protein ay gawa sa isa o higit pang polypeptides, na mga chain ng amino acids na pinagdugtong ng peptide bonds, at ang pagkakasunod-sunod ng amino acids ang tumutukoy kung paano tutupi ang protein.
copy.bis: Ang matag protein hinimo sa usa o daghan pang polypeptides, nga mga chain sa amino acids nga gidugtong sa peptide bonds, ug ang han-ay sa amino acids maoy nagtino kon giunsa pagtupi ang protein.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Natality, mortality, immigration, and emigration all change population size
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some effects of weather disturbances that occur in or near the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes factors that change population size (natality, mortality, immigration, emigration). This is population ecology, not weather disturbances in or near the Philippines. It does not support the competency in any way.

copy.en: Natality, mortality, immigration, and emigration all change population size by adding or removing individuals from a group.
copy.tl: Ang natality, mortality, immigration, at emigration ay nagpapabago sa laki ng population sa pamamagitan ng pagdaragdag o pagbawas ng mga indibidwal sa isang grupo.
copy.bis: Ang natality, mortality, immigration, ug emigration nag-usab sa gidak-on sa population pinaagi sa pagdugang o pagkuha sa mga indibidwal sa usa ka grupo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in the same area
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the ecological concept of population versus community. G3-F-2 is about forces affecting the movement of objects (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture). There is no connection to movement of objects or forces; the tag is from a completely different domain.

copy.en:
If you see ten tilapia fish in one pond, is that a community?

No, that's a population! A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in the same area, so all those tilapia together are one population.
copy.tl:
Kung makakita ka ng sampung tilapia sa isang lawa, community ba iyon?

Hindi, population iyon! Ang population ay grupo ng mga organism na magkakapareho ng species na naninirahan sa iisang lugar, kaya lahat ng tilapia na iyon ay isang population.
copy.bis:
Kung makakita ka ug napulo ka tilapia sa usa ka lanaw, community ba kana?

Dili, population kana! Ang population mao ang grupo sa mga organism nga pareho ug species nga nagpuyo sa samang lugar, busa kining tanang tilapia usa ka population.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because it is porous, meaning it has many tiny holes that can absorb or suck up water and soap.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why a sponge is porous and absorbs water/soap. It has no connection to PHIVOLCS volcano monitoring, alert levels, or volcanic eruption safety procedures. The assigned competency is entirely unrelated to the card content.

copy.en:
Why is a sponge used for cleaning dishes and wiping tables?

Because it is porous, meaning it has many tiny holes that can absorb or suck up water and soap.
copy.tl:
Bakit sponge ang ginagamit sa paghuhugas ng pinggan at pagpupunas ng mesa?

Kasi porous ito, ibig sabihin marami itong maliliit na butas na kayang sumipsip ng tubig at sabon.
copy.bis:
Ngano sponge ang gigamit sa paghugas sa mga plato ug pagpahid sa lamesa?

Tungod kay porous kini, buot ipasabot daghan kini og gagmay nga lungag nga makasuyop sa tubig ug sabon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Positive feedback amplifies a change, pushing the body further away from its starting state until a specific event is completed.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes positive feedback in biological homeostasis, which is unrelated to the competency about advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation (heat transfer).

copy.en: Positive feedback amplifies a change, pushing the body further away from its starting state until a specific event is completed.
copy.tl: Pinalalakas ng positive feedback ang isang pagbabago, kaya mas lalong lumalayo ang katawan mula sa panimulang estado hanggang matapos ang isang partikular na pangyayari.
copy.bis: Gipalig-on sa positive feedback ang usa ka pagbag-o, mao nga mas molayo pa ang lawas gikan sa sinugdanan nga estado hangtod mahuman ang usa ka partikular nga panghitabo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Potassium chloride, with the formula KCl, is an inorganic fertilizer that supplies potassium
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes potassium chloride as a fertilizer and nutrient source, which is chemistry/agriculture content. G9-F-7 requires guided investigations on current, voltage, and resistance in series and parallel circuits. There is no connection to electrical circuits.

copy.en: Potassium chloride, with the formula KCl, is an inorganic fertilizer that supplies potassium, an important nutrient for plant health.
copy.tl: Ang potassium chloride, na may pormulang KCl, ay isang inorganic fertilizer na nagbibigay ng potassium, isang mahalagang nutrient para sa kalusugan ng halaman.
copy.bis: Ang potassium chloride, nga adunay pormula nga KCl, usa ka inorganic fertilizer nga naghatag ug potassium, usa ka importante nga nutrient alang sa panglawas sa tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pounding is a strong force that hits a material, like a hammer flattening a piece of chalk into powder
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Pounding chalk into powder is a force/materials fact, not plant reproduction.

copy.en: Pounding is a strong force that hits a material, like a hammer flattening a piece of chalk into powder.
copy.tl: Ang pounding ay isang malakas na force na tumatama sa isang materyal, tulad ng martilyo na nagpapapisa sa isang piraso ng chalk hanggang maging pulbos.
copy.bis: Ang pounding usa ka kusgan nga force nga mohapak sa usa ka materyal, sama sa martilyo nga nagpapisa sa usa ka piraso sa chalk hangtod mahimong pulbos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Precision means your repeated measurements are close to each other
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines measurement precision; it contains no content about making objects move by natural causes or by pushing, pulling, rolling, or carrying. The assigned competency is about forces and motion, which is unrelated to the card's topic.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Precision means your repeated measurements are close to each other
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to demonstrate that pushes and pulls can be used to change the speed and direction of an object including making it go faster, turn it to a different direction, slow it down, and stop it
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains precision in measurements and does not address pushes and pulls changing speed or direction of an object. The competency is about demonstrating force effects on motion, which is not supported by the card.

copy.en:
What does it mean when my measurements are precise?

Precision means your repeated measurements are close to each other, even if they are not near the true value.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin kapag precise ang mga sukat ko?

Ang precision ay nangangahulugang magkakalapit ang mga paulit-ulit mong sukat, kahit hindi sila malapit sa totoong value.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pasabot kung precise ang akong mga sukod?

Ang precision nagpasabot nga ang imong gibalik-balik nga mga sukod duol sa usag usa, bisan dili sila duol sa tinuod nga value.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: upset the ecosystem's balance
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses predator-prey population dynamics and ecosystem balance, which is unrelated to the competency about waves carrying energy from a source to a receiver.

copy.en: If there are more predators, the animals that hunt other animals, in a community, the prey population may decrease too much and upset the ecosystem's balance.
copy.tl: Kung mas marami ang predators, ang mga hayop na nangangaso ng ibang hayop, sa isang komunidad, maaaring bumaba nang husto ang population ng prey at masira ang balanse ng ecosystem.
copy.bis: Kung mas daghan ang predators, ang mga mananap nga mangayam sa laing mananap, sa usa ka komunidad, mahimong momenos pag-ayo ang population sa prey ug maguba ang balanse sa ecosystem.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Predicting is using your observations to tell what will happen next
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: A science-process definition of predicting is unrelated to how plants reproduce.

copy.en:
What does it mean to predict in science?

Predicting is using your observations to tell what will happen next!
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng pag-predict sa science?

Ang predicting ay ang paggamit ng iyong mga obserbasyon para sabihin kung ano ang susunod na mangyayari!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang buot ipasabot sa pag-predict sa science?

Ang predicting mao ang paggamit sa imong mga obserbasyon aron pagsulti kon unsay sunod nga mahitabo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: 1 atm = 760 torr = 760 mm Hg and 1 atm = 101,325 Pa
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: create a scale drawing to represent relative thicknesses of the layers of Earth's interior, including the crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, outer core, and inner core
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches pressure unit conversions (atmospheres, torr, mm Hg, pascals). G9-E-8 requires creating a scale drawing of Earth's interior layers (crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, outer core, inner core). Pressure conversions have no relation to Earth's interior structure or scale drawing of its layers.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: 1 atm = 760 torr = 760 mm Hg and 1 atm = 101,325 Pa
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how seismic wave data has been used to develop a model for the internal structure and composition of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about pressure unit conversions, not about seismic wave data or the internal structure/composition of the Earth. It provides no information that supports describing how seismic wave data developed a model of Earth's interior.

copy.en: Pressure conversions include 1 atm = 760 torr = 760 mm Hg and 1 atm = 101,325 Pa.
copy.tl: Ang mga conversion ng pressure ay 1 atm = 760 torr = 760 mm Hg at 1 atm = 101,325 Pa.
copy.bis: Ang mga conversion sa pressure mao ang 1 atm = 760 torr = 760 mm Hg ug 1 atm = 101,325 Pa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the atmospheric pressure outside pushes the cup firmly against the surface
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to demonstrate that pushes and pulls can be used to change the speed and direction of an object including making it go faster, turn it to a different direction, slow it down, and stop it
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why a suction cup sticks due to atmospheric pressure, which is about static adhesion and pressure, not about pushes/pulls changing the speed or direction of an object. It does not support the competency's focus on changing motion (faster, slower, stop, turn).

copy.en:
Why does a suction cup stick so tightly?

When you press it, air inside gets pushed out. Then the atmospheric pressure outside pushes the cup firmly against the surface!
copy.tl:
Bakit malakas kumapit ang suction cup?

Kapag pinisil mo, lumalabas ang hangin sa loob. Sunod, itulak ng atmospheric pressure sa labas ang cup nang malakas sa ibabaw!
copy.bis:
Nganong hugot kaayo mo-dikit ang suction cup?

Kon pisilon nimo, mogawas ang hangin sa sulod. Dayon, iduso sa atmospheric pressure sa gawas ang cup nga hugot sa ibabaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Prevailing winds are the usual wind directions
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes prevailing winds and their causes (uneven heating, Earth's rotation). It does not address physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The topic is weather/climate, not matter properties.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Prevailing winds are the usual wind directions
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about prevailing winds, not the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume. No connection to states of matter or their shape/volume characteristics.

copy.en: Prevailing winds are the usual wind directions over a location, caused by uneven heating from the sun and the rotation of Earth on its axis.
copy.tl: Ang prevailing winds ay ang karaniwang direksyon ng hangin sa isang lugar, na dulot ng hindi pantay na pag-init ng araw at ng pag-ikot ng mundo sa axis nito.
copy.bis: Ang prevailing winds mao ang kasagarang direksyon sa hangin sa usa ka lugar, tungod sa dili patas nga pag-init sa adlaw ug sa pagtuyok sa kalibutan sa iyang axis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the three primary colors of paint you need are red, yellow, and blue!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the primary colors of paint (red, yellow, blue), which is about color mixing in art, not about sources of light, behavior of light, or uses of light. It does not support the G3-F-6 competency.

copy.en:
Which colors are the primary colors of paint?

When you paint, the three primary colors of paint you need are red, yellow, and blue!
copy.tl:
Anong mga kulay ang primaryong kulay ng pintura?

Kapag nagpipintura, ang tatlong primaryong kulay ng pintura na kailangan mo ay pula, dilaw, at asul!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga mga kolor ang panguna nga kolor sa pintura?

Kung nagpintura, ang tulo ka panguna nga kolor sa pintura nga imong gikinahanglan mao ang pula, dalag, ug asul!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The principal quantum number, written as n, tells you the main energy level of an electron
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw diagrams of and assemble series and parallel circuits, showing switch, battery, loads/resistors, ammeter, and voltmeter
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the principal quantum number, an atomic structure/chemistry concept. G9-F-8 requires drawing and assembling series and parallel circuits with specific components. There is no overlap in content; the card does not support the competency in any way.

copy.en: The principal quantum number, n, tells the main energy level or shell where an electron is found, with higher n meaning the electron is farther from the nucleus.
copy.tl: Ang principal quantum number, n, ay nagsasabi ng main energy level o shell kung saan matatagpuan ang isang electron, at mas mataas na n ay nangangahulugang mas malayo ang electron sa nucleus.
copy.bis: Ang principal quantum number, n, nag-ingon sa main energy level o shell diin makit-an ang usa ka electron, ug mas taas nga n nagpasabot nga mas layo ang electron sa nucleus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Every pregnancy has an equal chance of a Y-bearing sperm or an X-bearing sperm fertilizing the egg
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fifty percent each! Every pregnancy has an equal chance of a Y-bearing sperm or an X-bearing sperm fertilizing the egg
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: Sex-ratio probability is not how an interaction brings good or harm.

copy.en:
What is the chance of having a boy or a girl?

Fifty percent each! Every pregnancy has an equal chance of a Y-bearing sperm or an X-bearing sperm fertilizing the egg.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tsansa na magkaroon ng lalaki o babae?

Limampung porsyento bawat isa! Bawat pagbubuntis ay may pantay na tsansa na Y-bearing sperm o X-bearing sperm ang makapag-fertilize sa itlog.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang tsansa nga makabaton ug lalaki o babaye?

Singkwenta porsyento matag usa! Ang matag pagmabdos adunay patas nga tsansa nga Y-bearing sperm o X-bearing sperm ang maka-fertilize sa itlog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), gasoline, lubricating oil, and kerosene are organic compounds that come from petroleum and are used as fuels and lubricants.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes petroleum-derived products and their use as fuels and lubricants. G7-F-9 requires identifying advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation (heat transfer). The card contains no information about heat transfer mechanisms, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en: Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), gasoline, lubricating oil, and kerosene are organic compounds that come from petroleum and are used as fuels and lubricants.
copy.tl: Ang liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), gasoline, lubricating oil, at kerosene ay mga organic compound na mula sa petroleum at ginagamit bilang panggatong at pampadulas.
copy.bis: Ang liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), gasoline, lubricating oil, ug kerosene kay mga organic compound nga naggikan sa petroleum ug gigamit isip sugnod ug pangpadulas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: progesterone inhibits FSH and LH
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use diagrams and illustrations to describe the arrangement, spacing, and relative motion of the particles in each of the three states (phases) of matter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes hormonal regulation of the menstrual cycle (progesterone inhibiting FSH and LH), which has no connection to the particle model of matter or the arrangement, spacing, and motion of particles in states of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: progesterone inhibits FSH and LH
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the Particle Model of Matter as 'All matter is made up of tiny particles with each pure substance having its own kind of particles.'
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about reproductive hormones, not about the Particle Model of Matter or the idea that all matter is made of tiny particles. It does not support this competency in any way.

copy.en: During the luteal phase, progesterone inhibits FSH and LH, preventing new eggs from maturing while the uterus waits for a possible pregnancy.
copy.tl: Sa luteal phase, pinipigilan ng progesterone ang FSH at LH, kaya walang bagong itlog na nahihinog habang naghihintay ang uterus sa posibleng pagbubuntis.
copy.bis: Sa luteal phase, gipugngan sa progesterone ang FSH ug LH, busa walay bag-ong itlog nga mahinog samtang naghulat ang uterus sa posibleng pagmabdos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mixtures can be separated based on differences in properties such as density, magnetism, and how easily wind can carry a material away.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how high voltage electricity from power plants is generated and safely distributed to industries, businesses, and homes, including the role of substations (grid stations), and electric meters
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes separating mixtures using physical properties (density, magnetism, wind). This is a grade 6 chemistry topic (e.g., G6-M-6) and has no connection to high-voltage electricity generation and distribution, substations, or electric meters.

copy.en: Mixtures can be separated based on differences in properties such as density, magnetism, and how easily wind can carry a material away.
copy.tl: Ang mga mixture ay pwedeng paghiwalayin batay sa pagkakaiba ng properties tulad ng density, magnetism, at kung gaano kadaling tangayin ng hangin ang isang materyal.
copy.bis: Ang mga mixture pwede bulagon base sa kalainan sa mga properties sama sa density, magnetism, ug kung unsa kadali madala sa hangin ang usa ka materyal.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Metals show luster, meaning they are shiny, and they are also malleable, ductile, and good conductors of heat and electricity.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes physical properties of metals (non-living materials). G5-L-4 requires classifying living things (plants, animals, microorganisms) into groups using a table. There is no connection to living things or classification.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Metals show luster, meaning they are shiny, and they are also malleable, ductile, and good conductors of heat and electricity.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about metal properties, not about outer body parts of animals or their roles in movement and feeding. G3-L-4 is entirely unrelated to metals.

copy.en: Metals show luster, meaning they are shiny, and they are also malleable, ductile, and good conductors of heat and electricity.
copy.tl: Ang mga metal ay may luster, ibig sabihin makintab ang mga ito, at sila rin ay malleable, ductile, at mahusay na conductors ng init at kuryente.
copy.bis: Ang mga metal adunay luster, nagpasabot nga sinaw kini, ug sila usab malleable, ductile, ug maayo nga conductors sa init ug kuryente.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Prophase I of meiosis has five substages
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the substages of prophase I in meiosis, a biology topic. G6-M-4 is about uniform and non-uniform mixtures (solutions and suspensions) in matter. There is no instructional support for mixtures; the content is entirely unrelated.

copy.en: Prophase I of meiosis has five substages: leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, and diakinesis, where chromosomes pair and exchange segments.
copy.tl: Ang Prophase I ng meiosis ay may limang substages: leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, at diakinesis, kung saan nagpapares ang chromosomes at nagpapalitan ng segments.
copy.bis: Ang Prophase I sa meiosis adunay lima ka substages: leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, ug diakinesis, diin magpares ang chromosomes ug magbaylo og segments.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pollution, seawater contamination, and overuse can damage this valuable resource
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses threats to groundwater (pollution, seawater contamination, overuse) and the need to protect it. G8-L-2 requires using models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion. Groundwater is not a body system, and the card provides no information about organ systems or their interactions. The content is entirely unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
What threatens our groundwater?

Pollution, seawater contamination, and overuse can damage this valuable resource, so we must protect it.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagbabanta sa ating groundwater?

Ang pollution, seawater contamination, at overuse ay maaaring makasira sa mahalagang resource na ito, kaya dapat natin itong protektahan.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang naghulga sa atong groundwater?

Ang pollution, seawater contamination, ug overuse makadaot niining bililhon nga resource, busa kinahanglan nato kining panalipdan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: protect natural resources
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and describe some ways to use movement, sound, and light to send information between two people
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes actions to protect natural resources (planting trees, saving water, recycling, not throwing garbage). The competency G3-F-8 is about using movement, sound, and light to send information between two people. There is no connection to communication via movement, sound, or light.

copy.en: Individuals can help protect natural resources by doing simple things like planting trees, saving water, recycling, and not throwing garbage into rivers and seas.
copy.tl: Makakatulong ang bawat tao na protektahan ang natural resources sa pamamagitan ng simpleng mga bagay tulad ng pagtatanim ng puno, pagtitipid ng tubig, pag-recycle, at hindi pagtatapon ng basura sa ilog at dagat.
copy.bis: Makatabang ang matag tao sa pagprotektar sa natural resources pinaagi sa simple nga mga butang sama sa pagtanom ug kahoy, pagdaginot ug tubig, pag-recycle, ug dili paglabay ug basura sa suba ug dagat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wearing clothing that protects the skin on your hands and feet, like long sleeves and trousers, helps when working under the heat of the sun.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how homeostasis is maintained through various feedback mechanisms, both positive and negative
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a sun-safety measure (protective clothing), which is unrelated to homeostasis or feedback mechanisms. It does not support the competency's content about maintaining balance through positive/negative feedback.

copy.en: Wearing clothing that protects the skin on your hands and feet, like long sleeves and trousers, helps when working under the heat of the sun.
copy.tl: Ang pagsusuot ng damit na nagpoprotekta sa balat ng iyong mga kamay at paa, tulad ng long sleeves at trousers, ay nakakatulong kapag nagtatrabaho sa ilalim ng init ng araw.
copy.bis: Ang pagsul-ob og sinina nga makapanalipod sa panit sa imong mga kamot ug tiil, sama sa long sleeves ug trousers, makatabang kon magtrabaho ilalom sa init sa adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In the stomach, where gastric juices begin the chemical breakdown of proteins.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the chemical breakdown of proteins in the stomach, which is a digestive process. G6-M-1 requires describing changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) using diagrams and flowcharts. The card has no relation to states of matter or phase changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In the stomach, where gastric juices begin the chemical breakdown of proteins.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about protein digestion, not about how temperature changes cause matter to change state (solid to liquid to gas). It does not support the competency in any way.

copy.en:
Where does the body start breaking down proteins?

In the stomach, where gastric juices begin the chemical breakdown of proteins.
copy.tl:
Saan nagsisimulang tunawin ng katawan ang proteins?

Sa tiyan, kung saan sinisimulan ng gastric juices ang chemical breakdown ng proteins.
copy.bis:
Asa magsugod ang lawas sa pagtunaw sa proteins?

Sa tiyan, diin ang gastric juices magsugod sa chemical breakdown sa proteins.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: At the ribosomes! These tiny structures are the sites of protein synthesis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes ribosomes and protein synthesis, which is cell biology. G7-M-5 requires explaining changes of state (solid-liquid-vapor) in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes. No connection to matter or state changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: At the ribosomes! These tiny structures are the sites of protein synthesis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: G6-M-1 requires describing changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) using diagrams and flowcharts. The card is about ribosomes and protein synthesis, unrelated to matter or state changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: At the ribosomes! These tiny structures are the sites of protein synthesis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: G6-M-2 requires explaining the role of heat energy in change of state processes. The card discusses protein synthesis at ribosomes, with no mention of heat energy or state changes.

copy.en:
Where does the cell build its proteins?

At the ribosomes! These tiny structures are the sites of protein synthesis, like little factories.
copy.tl:
Saan gumagawa ng proteins ang cell?

Sa ribosomes! Ang maliliit na structures na ito ang sites ng protein synthesis, parang maliliit na pabrika.
copy.bis:
Asa maghimo ug proteins ang cell?

Sa ribosomes! Kining gagmay nga structures mao ang sites sa protein synthesis, sama sa gagmay nga pabrika.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Proteins are like tiny workers!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the functions of proteins in the human body (channels, hair/muscle, hormones, antibodies, enzymes). It contains no information about weather charts, weather characteristics, or safety precautions for poor/extreme weather, which are the focus of G4-E-6.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Proteins are like tiny workers!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in the weather can affect daily activities and explain how some types of weather can be dangerous for people
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about protein functions in the body, not about how weather changes affect daily activities or dangerous weather types. There is no connection to the weather-related competency G3-E-5.

copy.en:
Why does my body need proteins?

Proteins are like tiny workers! They form channels in cell membranes, build hair and muscle, act as hormones, fight germs as antibodies, and speed up reactions as enzymes.
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan ng katawan ko ng protina?

Ang mga protina ay parang maliliit na manggagawa! Bumubuo sila ng channels sa cell membrane, nagtatayo ng buhok at kalamnan, nagsisilbing hormones, lumalaban sa mikrobyo bilang antibodies, at nagpapabilis ng reaksyon bilang enzymes.
copy.bis:
Nganong kinahanglan sa akong lawas ang protina?

Ang mga protina sama sa gagmay nga mga trabahante! Naghimo sila ug channels sa cell membrane, nagtukod sa buhok ug kaunoran, nagsilbing hormones, nakig-away sa kagaw isip antibodies, ug nagpadali sa reaksyon isip enzymes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Proxima Centauri is located about 4.2 light-years away from our very own Sun!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks to describe the general structure of the solar system and identify major celestial objects within it. Proxima Centauri is a star outside the solar system; the card only states its distance from the Sun and provides no information about the solar system's structure, objects, features, or composition.

copy.en: Proxima Centauri is located about 4.2 light-years away from our very own Sun!
copy.tl: Ang Proxima Centauri ay nasa layong humigit-kumulang 4.2 taon-liwanag (light-years) mula sa Araw!
copy.bis: Ang Proxima Centauri mga 4.2 ka tuig-kahayag (light-years) ang gilay-on gikan sa Adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: pufferfish
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is a safety warning about not touching or eating a pufferfish. It does not use a drawing or diagram, and it does not classify Philippine animals/plants by habitat (terrestrial, aquatic, aerial). The content is unrelated to the competency's required classification activity.

copy.en: If you spot a pufferfish at the beach or market, tell a grown-up right away — never touch or eat it!
copy.tl: Kapag nakakita ka ng butete sa dalampasigan o palengke, sabihin agad sa matanda — huwag itong hawakan o kainin!
copy.bis: Kon makakita kag butete sa baybayon o merkado, sultihi dayon ang hamtong — ayaw kini hikapa o kan-a!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Puffing up and being poisonous are two different things
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses a misconception about pufferfish poison and puffing behavior. It does not describe any example of animals changing to better suit their environment, nor mimicry or camouflage. The content is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
Does puffing up make the pufferfish poisonous?

Puffing up and being poisonous are two different things — the pufferfish's poison stays inside its body all the time, even when it isn't puffed up.
copy.tl:
Galing ba sa paglaki ng butete ang lason nito?

Magkaiba ang paglaki ng butete at ang lason nito — nasa loob ng katawan nito ang lason kahit hindi ito namamaga.
copy.bis:
Gikan ba sa pagdako sa butete ang hilo niini?

Lahi ang pagdako sa butete ug ang hilo niini — anaa sa sulod sa lawas ang hilo bisan dili kini maghubag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth's gravity pulls all objects down toward its center
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss how bodies of water and landforms affect typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches that gravity pulls objects toward Earth's center, which is a physics/gravity concept. G8-E-9 is about how bodies of water and landforms affect typhoons, an Earth/space topic with no connection to gravity. The card provides no information about typhoons, bodies of water, or landforms.

copy.en: Earth's gravity pulls all objects down toward its center, regardless of the object's position or state of motion.
copy.tl: Hinihila ng gravity ng Earth ang lahat ng bagay pababa patungo sa gitna nito, anuman ang posisyon o estado ng paggalaw ng bagay.
copy.bis: Gibira sa gravity sa Earth ang tanang butang paubos padulong sa tunga niini, bisan unsa pa ang posisyon o kahimtang sa paglihok sa butang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You use a pulling force when you open a drawer
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches about pulling force in daily tasks, which is a force/motion topic. G3-M-9 requires identifying properties and uses of metals such as iron, gold, silver, and copper. There is no mention of metals or their properties, so the tag is unrelated.

copy.en: You use a pulling force when you open a drawer, pull a chair, or stretch a rubber band. Pulling moves an object toward you.
copy.tl: Gumagamit ka ng pulling force kapag binubuksan ang drawer, hinihila ang upuan, o iniuunat ang rubber band. Inilalapit ng paghila ang isang bagay sa iyo.
copy.bis: Gumagamit ka og pulling force kung imong ablihan ang drawer, ibira ang lingkuranan, o unat-unaton ang rubber band. Ang pagbira nagpaduol sa usa ka butang kanimo.
